title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Maine
description: Maine will elect one member to the U.S. Senate in 2026 for the Class II seat held by Republican Susan Collins. Collins is seeking another term against Democratic nominee Graham Platner, with Democratic write-in candidate Andrea LaFlamme also in the race. The contest is a competitive rematch between an entrenched incumbent and challengers running on change, affordability, and broader national political themes.

candidates.name: Graham Platner
candidates.summary: Graham Platner is a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Maine. His campaign says he is a Marine and U.S. Army veteran, an oyster farmer, and a former chair of the Sullivan Planning Board; Maine Public reported that he won the Democratic nomination to challenge Sen. Susan Collins in the 2026 general election.

Healthcare.stance: Platner says he supports moving from the current for-profit insurance system to Medicare for All, funding rural hospitals, allowing government negotiation of prescription drug prices, and opposing cuts to Medicare and Medicaid.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Economy.stance: Platner supports raising the federal minimum wage and indexing it to inflation, creating a billionaire minimum tax, backing unions and apprenticeship programs, and changing tax policy to reduce costs for working people and small businesses.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Climate/Energy.stance: Since mid-May 2026, Platner has released a more detailed energy plan that says the U.S. should move off fossil fuels, tax Big Oil windfall profits, freeze or lower electricity rates, eliminate federal gas and diesel taxes, and use federal financing plus the Defense Production Act to speed clean-energy, transmission, and grid projects. He also supports permitting reform for clean-energy buildout, a whole-home repair program to help households electrify and adopt heat pumps, and stronger climate action tied to lower consumer energy costs.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Platner supports a strong federal guarantee of the right to choose and says government should stay out of private reproductive decisions. He backs federal protections for abortion access.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Immigration.stance: Platner supports a path to citizenship, an end to mass deportations, and stronger border security as part of broader immigration reform.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Platner says he has not supported an assault-weapons ban in the form it has taken in past debates, and instead emphasizes safe storage, training, and limits on access for dangerous weapons. A November 2025 News Center Maine interview and the campaign platform both point to a more gun-safety-oriented approach rather than a blanket ban.

Foreign Policy.stance: Platner has condemned the war in Gaza and called for using every available means to bring it to an end, emphasizing peace, democracy, and self-determination. His platform says U.S. taxpayer dollars should not underwrite civilian suffering in Gaza.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Education.stance: Platner supports stronger federal support for public schools and says he would oppose federal support for private-school vouchers.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Tech & AI.stance: Platner says he would support legislation to restrict corporations' use of AI for surveillance, tracking, and predatory pricing, and he frames the issue as part of broader privacy and due-process protections.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Election Policy.stance: Platner supports a constitutional amendment to curb the influence of wealthy donors in elections and says current campaign finance rules allow billionaires to dominate politics.

sources.title: Platform — Graham Platner | Democrat for U.S. Senate

Local Issues.stance: Platner says Maine's housing crisis is existential and supports renewed federal support for housing construction, banning hedge funds from buying homes, expanding access to VA home loans, strengthening the working waterfront, and supporting tribal sovereignty.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Platner supports federal LGBTQ anti-discrimination legislation and says politicians should not use race, gender identity, or sexual orientation as political punching bags. He also says government should protect due process and civil liberties.

Available public record instead points to campaign positions and activism: his campaign platform and public statements emphasize anti-billionaire politics and organizing, and Maine Public and other coverage describe him as a political newcomer, oyster farmer, and Marine veteran rather than a current or former officeholder.
candidates.donor_summary: Raised about $16.31 million through May 20, 2026, according to FEC data, including about $16.11 million from individual contributions, nearly $9.68 million of that unitemized, plus about $174,684 from other committees and about $2.18 million cash on hand. OpenSecrets reported that labor-union PACs made up much of the growth in his PAC support, including a $10,000 contribution from an electrical workers union PAC and multiple $5,000 gifts from other labor PACs, while several billionaire donors gave comparatively small direct donations; OpenSecrets specifically reported $7,000 from George Soros, $7,000 from Pat Stryker, $5,000 from Jon Stryker, and $1,503 from Jennifer Pritzker, noting that the amounts came from FEC filings.

candidates.name: Susan Collins
candidates.summary: Susan Collins is the Republican incumbent U.S. senator from Maine, first elected in 1996 and seeking another term in 2026. Before joining the Senate, she worked for William Cohen, served in Maine state government, led the regional Small Business Administration office, and was founding executive director of the Center for Family Business at Husson College.

Economy.stance: Supports expanding workforce training and employer partnerships to connect unemployed or underemployed workers to good-paying jobs, including grants linking community and technical colleges with workforce boards, industry associations, and community groups. In recent 2026 statements, Collins also backed apprenticeship and Job Corps pipelines tied to Maine manufacturing and shipbuilding, framing them as investments in skilled labor, business growth, and economic security.

sources.title: Jobs & Economy | U.S. Senator Susan Collins
Senator Collins, Colleagues Reintroduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Workforce Training and Business Partnerships
Senators Collins, Reed Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Job Corps, U.S. Shipbuilding Workforce Pipeline
Senator Collins Delivers Keynote Address at Maine Manufacturers Annual Summit

Climate/Energy.stance: Collins says she supports reducing greenhouse gas emissions and expanding clean-energy jobs while preserving U.S. manufacturing and lowering energy costs for Maine households and businesses. She has also pushed for federal home-heating assistance and other measures aimed at easing energy costs in a state with heavy reliance on heating oil.

sources.title: Energy & Environment | U.S. Senator Susan Collins
Senator Collins Announces Release of More than $4.3 Million in Additional Federal Home Heating Aid for Mainers

Healthcare.stance: Supports bipartisan health-care reforms focused on affordability and access. Since May 2026, Collins has promoted the INSULIN Act to cap insulin costs at $35 per month for people with private or employer-sponsored insurance and create a pilot program to provide insulin at the same price for uninsured Americans, while also backing the Improving Access to Medicare Coverage Act to count hospital 'observation status' toward Medicare’s three-day requirement for skilled nursing coverage and reduce seniors’ out-of-pocket costs.

sources.title: Health Care | U.S. Senator Susan Collins
Senator Collins Praises Growing Senate Support for INSULIN Act
Senators Collins, Welch Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Seniors from High Cost of Post-Hospitalization Care

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Collins says abortion rights should be consistent nationally and has backed legislation to codify the core holdings of Roe v. Wade while allowing some post-viability restrictions and preserving conscience protections for providers with religious objections. She has also said access to contraception should be protected in federal law.

sources.title: Senator Collins Joins Bipartisan Effort to Codify Roe v. Wade
Senator Collins’ Statement on SCOTUS’ Dobbs Decision

Immigration.stance: Collins says immigrants in the country legally should not be targeted by ICE investigations and should be able to go to work, school, and public places without disruption. She also says people in the country illegally who have engaged in criminal activity may be subject to arrest and deportation, and she has backed funding for ICE body cameras and de-escalation training.

sources.title: Senator Collins' Statement on ICE Operations in Maine
Homeland Security | U.S. Senator Susan Collins

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Supports bipartisan gun-safety measures such as expanded background checks for some young adults, crisis-intervention programs, and efforts to reduce straw purchasing and firearms trafficking while preserving gun rights for lawful owners. Her Senate website describes her as working on bipartisan gun-safety legislation.

sources.title: Bipartisan Gun Safety Legislation Negotiated by Senator Collins and 11 Colleagues Advances

Foreign Policy.stance: Supports congressional oversight of military action and has broken with GOP leadership on some war-powers votes, including a 2026 vote to advance a resolution concerning U.S. military action in Iran. Her record suggests a preference for limiting unilateral executive war-making authority.

sources.title: Collins breaks with GOP leaders on Iran war powers resolution

Education.stance: Supports early childhood education, public K-12 schools, and making higher education more affordable. Her Senate issue page says she has a strong record of supporting education at all levels.

sources.title: Education | U.S. Senator Susan Collins

Tech & AI.stance: Collins supports federal limits on materially deceptive AI-generated election content and has backed efforts to let election officials use federal funds to counter AI-driven disinformation. She frames these proposals as protecting election integrity while preserving First Amendment exceptions for parody, satire, and news use.

sources.title: Senator Collins, Bipartisan Group Introduce Bill to Ban Deceptive AI-Generated Content in Elections

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Collins says transgender people should be treated with respect and dignity, but she supports interpreting Title IX on the basis of sex rather than gender identity in school athletics. In 2025, she signed a petition for a Maine referendum that would designate school sports teams and certain facilities by sex assigned at birth and said the policy would promote fair competition for girls and women.

sources.title: Sen. Collins signs petition for 'Protect Girls Sports' referendum
Sen. Susan Collins signs petition for 'Protect Girls Sports in Maine' referendum

Election Policy.stance: Collins has supported two different bills called the SAVE Act: a 2017 measure focused on election-system security and information-sharing, and a 2026 proposal called the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act. In 2026, she said she supported a one-time documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement at voter registration and photo ID for voting in federal races, while opposing a version that would require proof every time a ballot is cast.

Local Issues.stance: Collins highlights targeted federal investments in Maine communities, including infrastructure, rural health, child care, housing, public safety, and workforce projects across all 16 counties. She has also defended Maine’s lobster industry by opposing a broad federal shift to mandatory ropeless gear and urging a more flexible approach developed with fishermen and state regulators.

candidates.voting_summary: Collins is the incumbent U.S. senator from Maine and, according to GovTrack, had missed 0 of 10,011 roll call votes from January 1997 through June 2026. GovTrack also lists recently enacted bills she sponsored, including the District of Columbia Local Funds Act, 2025 and the Electoral Count Reform and Presidential Transition Improvement Act of 2022. PolitiFact reported that CQ Roll Call found Collins voted with President Donald Trump's position 94.6% of the time in 2025, while also noting she broke with him on key votes such as opposing the 2025 Senate reconciliation bill over Medicaid and rural health concerns.

candidates.donor_summary: Raised about $12.17 million for the 2025–2026 period through May 20, 2026 on her FEC candidate page, while OpenSecrets reported $10.28 million raised through the March 31, 2026 filing and roughly $10.0 million cash on hand at that point. OpenSecrets and Maine Monitor reporting indicate backing from finance and investment-world donors, especially billionaire donors connected to hedge funds and private equity; Maine Monitor identified $2.5 million from Citadel founder Ken Griffin and $2 million from Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman to the pro-Collins Pine Tree Results PAC, while Collins’ broader network drew about $9.8 million from nearly 100 billionaires and spouses. FEC and OpenSecrets also show substantial committee and transfer support, including about $1.54 million in other-committee contributions and about $3.97 million in transfers from authorized committees on the FEC overview page.

flags.concern: LaFlamme's Tech & AI stance is marked 'low' confidence and notes 'no public position found.' The closest related position cited is opposition to data centers as part of environmental policy. This is appropriately documented as a gap rather than a fabricated position, which is correct methodology.

Platner's firearms stance is marked 'medium' confidence and states he 'has not supported an assault-weapons ban in the form it has taken in past debates' and emphasizes 'safe storage, training, and limits on access for dangerous weapons.' The sources cited are his campaign platform and a November 2025 News Center Maine interview. The phrasing 'has not supported' could be slightly clearer—it would benefit from explicit confirmation that this represents his current position rather than a past position he has since changed, though the sourcing appears solid.
flags.suggestion: Consider clarifying whether this represents a long-standing position or a recent shift in stance, if the sources support such detail.

flags.concern: Collins' Civil Rights stance on transgender issues is sourced to two news articles (WMTW, WABI-TV) reporting that she signed a petition for a Maine referendum on school sports. The sources describe her as supporting 'fair competition for girls and women' and the policy as designating 'school sports teams and certain facilities by sex assigned at birth.' This is factually documented, but the framing—'Collins says transgender people should be treated with respect and dignity, but she supports interpreting Title IX on the basis of sex rather than gender identity'—presents both a positive statement and a policy position. The positive framing is not contradicted by the sources, but readers should note this represents Collins' own stated values alongside her policy position.

Platner's donor summary notes that OpenSecrets reported billionaire donations ($7,000 from George Soros, $7,000 from Pat Stryker, $5,000 from Jon Stryker, $1,503 from Jennifer Pritzker) while emphasizing that 'labor-union PACs made up much of the growth in his PAC support.' This framing is neutral and factually sourced, but it's worth noting that the profile explicitly contextualizes small billionaire donations within a larger small-dollar, labor-backed fundraising picture—which is appropriate given Platner's anti-billionaire campaign messaging.

Collins' voting summary cites GovTrack data showing she 'had missed 0 of 10,011 roll call votes from January 1997 through June 2026' and PolitiFact reporting she 'voted with President Donald Trump's position 94.6% of the time in 2025.' The PolitiFact source appropriately notes she 'broke with him on key votes such as opposing the 2025 Senate reconciliation bill over Medicaid and rural health concerns.' This is well-balanced and sourced, but the 94.6% figure is a single-year snapshot (2025) and may not represent her full career alignment with Trump. The profile handles this correctly by attributing it to 2025 specifically.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the 2026 Maine Senate race with strong documentation across all three candidates. The profile demonstrates excellent internal consistency: candidate positions are clearly sourced to official campaign websites, Senate records, and credible news outlets (Maine Public, The Hill, PolitiFact, Maine Monitor). Career histories are documented and align with cited sources. The language is notably neutral and balanced across candidates—each candidate's stance is described using their own framing (e.g., 'pro-choice' for Platner, 'codify Roe v. Wade' for Collins) rather than loaded terminology. Polling data includes sample sizes and source URLs. The profile appropriately flags low-confidence stances (e.g., LaFlamme on Tech & AI) where no public position was found after a good-faith search. Minor areas for enhancement noted below, but no factual errors or systematic bias detected.
